newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL-Trading quiet ahead of book-to-bill.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL-Trading quiet ahead of book-to-bill.

text.p: Traders said on Monday after-hours activity was quiet because of the U.S. Veterans Day holiday as well as the Semiconductor Industry Association's monthly book-to-bill report which was expected later this evening.
They said investors were waiting for the October book-to-bill figure, anticipation of which helped send the technology-heavy Nasdaq to a record high during market hours, up 5.17 points to 1262.68.
After the SIA released the October ratio figure of 1.10, the highest level since December, 1995, shares of both Intel Corp and Micron Technology Inc jumped higher.
Intel shares gained one to 124-7/8. The stock had gained 1-5/8 during the day.
Micron shares rose 7/8 to 32-3/4, traders said, after gaining 1-7/8 during regular market hours.
The New York Stock Exchange said its session one volume was 2,300 shares compared with 1,600 shares on Friday. There was no session two volume today or on Friday.
The American Stock Exchange said there was no after-hours activity.
